source: Realmz struct offsetof probe, Oracle fixture proof, runtime consumers, and local output corpus

realmzSourceAnchors.finding: The record contains 20 rectangles, percent values, battle ranges, three random doors and percents, landlook, darkness, LOS, only flags, option bytes, sounds, and text IDs.
CvtRandLevelToPc converts rects, short arrays, booleans, sounds, and text; landlook and option are byte fields.
Runtime checks rectangles from index 19 down to 0, tests Rand(10000) <= percent, fires extra AP doors, optionally prompts using option/sound/text, then picks battle range.
A movement path checks rectangles where percent < 0 and can fire extra AP doors without the normal random-battle flow.
Opcodes 23, -23, 92, and 106 mutate random rectangle percent/ranges/shape or level landlook/darkness.

layout.editorMeaning: Chance in times per 10000; negative values use a seamless-door path.
Up to three extra Action Point door IDs.
Chance out of 100 for each extra AP; positive one-shot, negative repeat.
Stop lower-priority random rectangle checks when party is inside this rectangle.
Prompt/surprise chance used before random battle.
Preserve native alignment byte without decoding it as sound data.
Data SD2 message ID displayed with option prompt.

runtimeSemantics.priority: Rectangles are checked from index 19 down to 0.
runtimeSemantics.percent: Rand(10000) <= percent; label as times in 10000.
runtimeSemantics.extraApPercent: Rand(100) <= abs(randdoorpercent); positive values are zeroed after firing, negative values repeat.
runtimeSemantics.only: If true, random checks stop after this rectangle is processed.
runtimeSemantics.option: Rand(100) < option triggers sound/text prompt and can set favorable surprise before battle.
runtimeSemantics.negativePercent: Supported by Realmz source for seamless extra-AP checks; not observed in local output corpus.

editorImplications: Validate percent as times in 10000, not percent out of 100.
Show rectangle priority order and warn on overlap only when it affects expected behavior.
Expose positive extra AP percent as one-shot and negative extra AP percent as repeat.
Rename option UI to prompt/surprise chance and link sound/text to decoded targets.
Treat opcodes 23, -23, 92, and 106 as runtime mutation evidence when they alter random-level data.
